catalog.title: Paolina Borghese Bonaparte as Venus Victorious
catalog.dimensions: H 92 cm; H 160 cm including the bed
catalog.note: Canova portrays Paolina Bonaparte as Venus, reclining on an intricately carved bed and holding the apple awarded to the goddess in the Judgment of Paris.
catalog.scan_source: Independent community photogrammetry capture published publicly and savable on Polycam under CC BY 4.0.

work_rights.assessment: Public-domain historical artwork; independent scan licensed CC BY4.0
work_rights.basis: Original marble made 1804–1808; Antonio Canova died in 1822.

object_identity_evidence: Distinctive bed, reclining portrait, apple, and drapery match the Galleria Borghese original named in the capture title. Museum inventory LIV identifies the marble, rather than the plaster at Possagno.
content_review: Adult portrait subject: the museum identifies Paolina as born in 1780 and the work as 1804–1808. Reclining, partly draped adult figure; no sex act, child, violence, or coercive interaction.
cautions: Original capture includes a large museum-floor rectangle outside the bed. Conservative cleanup requested; use only an accepted cleaned preview after full-model QA.
English introductory prose has an inconsistent ending date of 1810; the Italian text and both structured museum records state 1804–1808, consistent with payment in May 1808.

catalog.title: Mars and Venus
catalog.note: Mars supports the wounded Venus in an episode from Homer’s Iliad. Sergel began the group in Rome in 1775 and completed it in Stockholm in 1804, shaping the two figures to be seen from every side.
